source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); (AJ) Military Retirement Credit (PDF p.23) and worksheet lines 1 and 2 (PDF p.24); Line 8 subtractions, a closed list (PDF p.10)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 30,000.00 + public pension paid by federal (person 0) 30,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 60,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 60,000.00 + 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 60,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 10 = 60,000.00 x 0.045 = 2,700.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 60,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 41,787.00. Line 19 = 41,787.00 x 0.013 = 543.231. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 543.231) = 401.769. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 44,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 401.769 = 401.769; credits 401.77. Tax = 2,700.00 - 401.77 = 2,298.23. Military retirement pay 'does not include ... non-military federal retirement' (PDF p.23), so no AJ and no subtraction. Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
